title: Five-colourability when odd cycles pairwise intersect
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. Suppose that every two odd cycles of $G$ share a vertex; that is, for any two closed walks in $G$ that are cycles of odd length, there is a vertex lying on both. Then the chromatic number of $G$ satisfies $\chi(G) \le 5$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
every pair of odd cycles has a common vertex
replaced:
\emph{Show that if any two odd cycles of \texttt{G}
have a vertex in common, then \texttt{$\chi$ $\le$ 5}.}
